newsitem.title: ALBANIA: ALBANIA'S LONG-EXILED KING TO VISIT REBEL CITY.
newsitem.headline: ALBANIA'S LONG-EXILED KING TO VISIT REBEL CITY.

text.p: Albania's long-exiled King Leka I, who is trying to unify the violence-stricken Balkan state, is planning a trip to the rebel-held southern city of Vlore on Thursday, a spokesman for the monarchist party said.
"I am positive that the people of Vlore will give Leka a warm welcome," Guri Durollari, chairman of the Legality Movement Party, told reporters.

He said Leka, who returned from exile in South Africa this month to urge the restoration of the monarchy, would meet Vlore residents but did not plan to contact the rebel committee which controls the Adriatic port city.
Leka, 58, has appealed for peace and unity in Albania, which sank into near-anarchy after the failure of fraudulent savings plans earlier this year.
Rebel committees, which reject the authority of President Sali Berisha, control much of the south. They say Berisha, a northerner, is responsible for the failure of the savings schemes.
Leka was not planning to take any special security measures in Vlore, Durollari said.
"We will be meeting our brothers and sisters, so there is no need to be worried," he said.
Last Sunday Leka paid a triumphal visit to his ancestral village north of the capital Tirana. More than 5,000 people turned out to welcome him.
Leka was two days old when his father, King Zog, fled with his family in 1939 ahead of invading Italian fascists.
